author: template-projects
name: Aspire starter add-on: Wolverine event sourcing
description: Adds a Wolverine event-sourcing slice - aggregate handlers, a transactional outbox and an async projection - on the event store that matches the base scaffold's data store: Marten on PostgreSQL, Polecat on SQL Server 2025, or Fisher on SQLite. Emits one .scaffold/aspire-events.<store>.wiring.md, which lists the solution, AppHost and package-version edits the scaffolding skill applies.

resource.description: The singular PascalCase name of the sample resource, e.g. Product. The scaffold's entity, controller, page and tests are named from it. The plural is this plus "s" - an irregular plural is a rename after scaffolding, not a second parameter. Pass the SAME value to every template in a scaffold, exactly like -n.

resourceLower.//: The lowercase form, for TypeScript identifiers, route paths and file names. A separate symbol because `replaces` is a literal substitution - unlike sourceName, it does not match case variants.

eventStore.description: Which event store backs the slice. This is not an independent choice: it must match the base scaffold's --dbProvider, because the AppHost only declares the events service when Database:Provider agrees with it. dotnet new cannot pass a symbol between two template invocations, which is why it has to be stated again here.

choices.description: Pair with --dbProvider postgres. Its own events-pg container, separate from the API's store.

Pair with --dbProvider sqlserver. A second database on the API's SQL Server, which the AppHost pins to 2025-latest for Polecat's native json type. Adds an optional Azure Service Bus transport, off by default.
Pair with --dbProvider sqlite. A local file and no container, so the scaffold still needs no Docker at all.

modifiers.//: azurerm_container_app declares a block whose name is exactly this template's sourceName, so substitution would rename it and the configuration would stop parsing. The file needs no substitution of its own - every name in it comes from a Terraform local. servicebus.tf carries no such block and is substituted normally.

One host project per event store, and only one of them ships. They cannot be a single project with conditional regions: each store declares its own IDocumentSession, SingleStreamProjection and [AggregateHandler], and JasperFx.Events ships a source generator that emits a type per projection, so a project referencing two stores fails to compile. src/shared/ carries everything store-agnostic, always survives, and is linked into the surviving host rather than referenced as an assembly - see its README.
One wiring file per store, for the same reason: the AppHost block, the package versions and the appsettings keys all differ. Exactly one reaches the scaffold's .scaffold/ directory.
